History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
• 64-year-old woman with diabetes and hypertension presents via telehealth with a 5-day history of dry cough and copious nasal discharge, clinically consistent with a probable viral upper respiratory tract infection; safety-netting advice given.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Dry cough every 20–30 minutes and continuous “streaming” nasal discharge for 5 days.  
• Timeline/progression: Symptoms began ≈5 days ago; no significant improvement yet.  
• Character: Cough is dry; nasal discharge described as green.  
• Associated symptoms:
  – Intermittent subjective fevers with alternating chills and feeling “very hot” (temperature not yet checked).  
  – Generalized myalgia.  
  – Brief episode of diarrhoea at symptom onset, now resolved.  
  – Denies chest pain, pleuritic pain, dyspnoea, wheeze (except with intense exercise), haemoptysis, sore throat, ear pain, headaches, visual change, vomiting, current diarrhoea, rash, urinary frequency, polyuria or polydipsia.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Lemsip (paracetamol-containing hot drink) 2–3/day provides transient throat relief; no other OTC medications taken.  
• Systems review: Otherwise unremarkable as per above negatives.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus – HbA1c “normal” on recent labs (≈3 weeks ago).  
  – Medication: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Hypertension – stability of BP unclear (last check “a while ago”).  
  – Medication: Lisinopril 200 mg? (dose/route/frequency not clearly documented – “two-hundred”).  
• No chronic lung disease; no history of recurrent chest infections.

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.  
• Seasonal hay fever noted (non-drug).

Social History:
• Lives with partner and a dog.  
• Occupation: Office manager.  
• Alcohol: “The odd sherry.”  
• Smoking: Not documented.  
• Illicit drugs: Not mentioned.  
• Height 5 ft 5 in; weight 65 kg (BMI ≈24).

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Telehealth visit – no physical exam performed; no vital signs available.

Investigations:
• None performed during this consult.  
• Recent diabetes blood test ≈3 weeks ago reported as “normal” (no values provided).

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Acute cough & rhinorrhoea, likely viral URTI/bronchitis vs early bacterial infection
  • Plan:
    – Obtain thermometer; check and record temperature at home.  
    – Symptomatic relief: continue Lemsip (contains paracetamol); avoid other paracetamol-containing products.  
    – Encourage hydration, rest, and allow cough during daytime; limited use of cough syrup only if night-time cough prevents sleep.  
    – Safety-net: Re-consult if temperature ≥ 37.5–38 °C persists or spikes, cough worsens, develop purulent sputum, haemoptysis, nasal bleeding, chest pain, or shortness of breath.

Issue 2 – Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
  • Plan:
    – Continue metformin as prescribed.  
    – Monitor for hyperglycaemia during illness (patient currently lacks home glucose testing; advised to ensure regular GP monitoring).  
    – Attend routine diabetic reviews as scheduled by GP.

Issue 3 – Hypertension
  • Plan:
    – Continue lisinopril; confirm correct dose with GP/pharmacy.  
    – Arrange routine blood pressure monitoring with GP.

General Plan Items
  • Review if any red-flag symptoms develop or no improvement in 1–2 weeks.  
  • Advise patient to maintain scheduled follow-ups for chronic conditions.

Quality checks:
• Missing/expected data:     – No smoking status recorded.     – Full medication list with doses/frequencies incomplete.     – No allergy cross-check beyond drugs (food/latex not asked).     – No vital signs or physical exam due to teleconsult. • Internal conflicts: none identified. • Transcript quality: clear; minor conversational fillers; no significant inaudible sections.
